$comment: Nuclear Tutorials catalogue seed. Structure: institution -> course (semester 1|2) -> video lessons. Lesson videos are curated public lecture series (MIT OpenCourseWare CC BY-NC-SA, Crash Course) and link back to the original source; titles, topics and durations match those sources. Administrators add, edit, reorder, publish and remove lessons from Admin -> Video lessons without touching this file.

institutions.name: University of Zambia
institutions.summary: Zambia's oldest public university (founded 1966). Engineering, natural sciences and computer studies programmes.

courses.title: Mathematics I: Single Variable Calculus
courses.description: Limits, derivatives and the rules of differentiation, built up lecture by lecture for first-year students.

videos.title: Rates of Change, Slope, Velocity and the Derivative
videos.description: The derivative is introduced as a rate of change from geometry and physics examples. MIT OpenCourseWare, Single Variable Calculus (Fall 2007), CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Limits and Continuity
videos.description: How limits are defined and evaluated, and what it means for a function to be continuous. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Derivatives of Products and Quotients
videos.description: The product rule and quotient rule, with worked examples and proofs. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: The Chain Rule and Higher Derivatives
videos.description: Differentiating composite functions and interpreting second derivatives. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Implicit Differentiation and Inverse Functions
videos.description: Differentiating implicitly defined curves and the derivatives of inverse functions. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Exponentials, Logarithms and Logarithmic Differentiation
videos.description: The exponential and logarithm functions, their derivatives and logarithmic differentiation. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

courses.title: Physics I: Classical Mechanics
courses.description: Units, kinematics, vectors, Newton's laws and simple harmonic motion — the mechanics core of first-year physics.

videos.title: Powers of Ten, Units, Dimensions and Uncertainty
videos.description: Measurement, units, dimensional analysis and uncertainty in physical experiments. Lectures by Walter Lewin, MIT 8.01 Classical Mechanics.

videos.title: One-Dimensional Kinematics: Speed, Velocity, Acceleration
videos.description: Position, displacement, average and instantaneous velocity in one dimension. Lectures by Walter Lewin, MIT 8.01.

videos.title: Vectors: Dot Products, Cross Products, 3D Kinematics
videos.description: Vector algebra and its use in describing motion in two and three dimensions. Lectures by Walter Lewin, MIT 8.01.

videos.title: Circular Motion and Centripetal Forces
videos.description: Uniform circular motion, centripetal acceleration and perceived gravity. Lectures by Walter Lewin, MIT 8.01.

videos.title: Newton's Laws of Motion
videos.description: Inertia, force, action and reaction, with classroom demonstrations. Lectures by Walter Lewin, MIT 8.01.

videos.title: Hooke's Law, Springs, Pendulums and Simple Harmonic Motion
videos.description: Restoring forces, oscillation, period and energy in simple harmonic systems. Lectures by Walter Lewin, MIT 8.01.

courses.title: Introduction to Programming in Python
courses.description: Computation, branching, iteration and program design for students with no programming background.

videos.title: What is Computation?
videos.description: What computation is, how a program describes it, and how Python executes it. MIT OpenCourseWare, 6.0001 (Fall 2016), CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Branching and Iteration
videos.description: Conditional statements and loops as the two structures that make programs do work. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: String Manipulation, Guess and Check, Approximations, Bisection
videos.description: Working with strings and writing iterative approximations, including bisection search. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

courses.title: Linear Algebra
courses.description: Systems of linear equations, elimination, vector spaces, independence and the four fundamental subspaces.

videos.title: The Geometry of Linear Equations
videos.description: Linear equations seen as planes, rows and columns of a matrix. MIT OpenCourseWare, 18.06 Linear Algebra (Spring 2005), CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Elimination with Matrices
videos.description: Gaussian elimination written as matrix operations, with back substitution. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Transposes, Permutations and Vector Spaces
videos.description: Permutation matrices, transposes and the definition of a vector space. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Column Space and Nullspace
videos.description: The two subspaces attached to every matrix and what solvability means. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Independence, Basis and Dimension
videos.description: Linear independence, span, bases and the dimension of a subspace. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: The Four Fundamental Subspaces
videos.description: Column space, nullspace, row space and left nullspace, and how their dimensions relate. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

courses.title: Introduction to Nuclear Engineering and Radiation
courses.description: Nuclear stability, binding energy, reaction notation, cross sections and radioactive decay — the foundation of nuclear science.

videos.title: Radiation History and the Discovery of the Neutron
videos.description: From early radiation research to the discovery of the neutron, and why it matters today. MIT OpenCourseWare, 22.01 (Fall 2016), CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Nuclear Mass and Stability, Reaction Notation and Cross Sections
videos.description: Mass as energy, nuclear stability trends, reaction notation and per-particle reaction probability. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Binding Energy and the Semi-Empirical Liquid Drop Model
videos.description: Binding energy per nucleon, the liquid drop model and mass parabolas. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Mass Parabolas, Stability and Half Life
videos.description: Reading stability from mass parabolas and the meaning of half life. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: The Q-Equation: The Most General Nuclear Reaction
videos.description: Energy release in nuclear reactions derived from conservation laws. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Radioactive Decay: Modes, Energetics and Trends
videos.description: Alpha, beta and gamma decay, decay energetics and the trends behind the decay chart. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

institutions.name: Copperbelt University
institutions.summary: Zambia's second-largest public university, founded 1987, with a focus on engineering, technology and business.

courses.title: Mathematical Methods I
courses.description: Approximation, curve sketching, optimisation, related rates and the definite integral for engineering students.

videos.title: Linear and Quadratic Approximations
videos.description: Using the derivative to approximate functions near a point. MIT OpenCourseWare, Single Variable Calculus, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Curve Sketching
videos.description: Using first and second derivatives to sketch and read graphs. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Maximum-Minimum Problems
videos.description: Applied optimisation: finding extreme values in real engineering problems. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Related Rates
videos.description: Rates that depend on each other, solved by differentiating a relation. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Definite Integrals
videos.description: The definite integral as a limit of Riemann sums, with its properties. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: The First Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
videos.description: How differentiation and integration undo each other, and what that gives you. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

courses.title: Analog Circuits and Electronics
courses.description: Sinusoidal steady state, impedance, filters, operational amplifiers and energy in electronic circuits.

videos.title: Sinusoidal Steady State
videos.description: How circuits behave when driven by sinusoidal sources, and why this matters. MIT OpenCourseWare, 6.002 Circuits and Electronics, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: The Impedance Model
videos.description: Extending resistive analysis to capacitors and inductors through impedance. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Filters
videos.description: Frequency-selective circuits built from impedance and analysis. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: The Operational Amplifier Abstraction
videos.description: Why the op-amp is the standard building block for analog design. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Operational Amplifier Circuits
videos.description: Amplifiers, summers and integrators built from op-amps. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Op Amps with Positive Feedback
videos.description: Comparator and Schmitt trigger behaviour when feedback is positive. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

institutions.name: Mulungushi University
institutions.summary: Public university in Kabwe, Central Province, offering science, agriculture, business and education programmes.

courses.title: Principles of Chemical Science
courses.description: Atomic structure, wave-particle duality, orbital energies, periodic trends and bonding.

videos.title: Atomic Structure
videos.description: The experimental evidence that shaped the modern model of the atom. MIT OpenCourseWare, 5.111 Principles of Chemical Science (Fall 2014), CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Wave-Particle Duality of Light
videos.description: Light behaving as both wave and particle, and what spectroscopy reveals. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Wave-Particle Duality of Matter and the Schrödinger Equation
videos.description: Matter waves, the wavefunction and how energy levels emerge. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Hydrogen Atom Energy Levels
videos.description: Quantised energy levels of hydrogen and how they are calculated. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: The Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
videos.description: Atomic size, ionisation energy and electron affinity explained from orbital structure. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

videos.title: Lewis Structures
videos.description: Drawing Lewis structures to describe bonding and molecular shape. MIT OpenCourseWare, CC BY-NC-SA.

courses.title: Statistics Foundations
courses.description: What statistics is for, how to reason with numbers, and how to describe data with averages and spread.

videos.title: What Is Statistics?
videos.description: Why statistics matter, what they can answer, and how they are misused. Crash Course Statistics.

videos.title: Mathematical Thinking and Numeracy
videos.description: Reading very large and very small numbers, and visualising data honestly. Crash Course Statistics.

videos.title: Mean, Median and Mode: Measures of Central Tendency
videos.description: The three common averages, when each is appropriate, and how they can mislead. Crash Course Statistics.

institutions.name: Secondary School Programme
institutions.summary: The Nuclear Tutorials secondary pathway: exam-focused video lessons for Grades 10 to 12, organised in two school semesters.

courses.title: Chemistry Essentials
courses.description: Atoms, the nucleus, significant figures, the fundamental laws of chemistry and reading the periodic table.

videos.title: The Nucleus and the Atom
videos.description: Protons, neutrons and electrons, atomic number, isotopes and relative atomic mass. Crash Course Chemistry.

videos.title: Unit Conversion and Significant Figures
videos.description: SI units, scientific notation and reporting measurements with the right precision. Crash Course Chemistry.

videos.title: The Fundamental Laws of Chemistry
videos.description: Conservation of mass, compounds and the birth of modern chemistry. Crash Course Chemistry.

videos.title: The Periodic Table
videos.description: How Mendeleev's table is organised and how to read the information inside it. Crash Course Chemistry.

courses.title: Physics Essentials
courses.description: Motion, the calculus of physics, vectors and Newton's laws, explained for school learners.

videos.title: Motion in a Straight Line
videos.description: Displacement, velocity and acceleration with everyday examples. Crash Course Physics.

videos.title: Derivatives in Physics
videos.description: How gradients and rates of change describe motion. Crash Course Physics.

videos.title: Integrals in Physics
videos.description: Using areas under graphs to find distance travelled. Crash Course Physics.

videos.title: Vectors and Two-Dimensional Motion
videos.description: Scalars, vectors and projectile motion. Crash Course Physics.

videos.title: Newton's Laws of Motion
videos.description: Force, mass, acceleration and action-reaction pairs. Crash Course Physics.
